measurement: a one-sided numeric screen that refutes candidates before they are proved
why: Batching pays only while (1-p)^b > 1/b (results/lean_batching_bisection.json), so an evolutionary search -- which fails most candidates by construction -- sits where batching costs MORE than verifying one at a time. That bound assumes falsity is discoverable only by proving. It is not: disagreement at one rational point refutes an identity, and all b candidates are evaluated inside ONE invocation, so the false ones leave before the proof batch is formed.

soundness.a_refutation: a witness of inequality, and final -- no proof of a false identity exists
soundness.a_survivor: has only failed to be refuted, and still faces the real Lean gate
soundness.therefore: the screen can subtract work but can never grant acceptance, so it adds no trust surface
soundness.demonstrated_not_asserted: tests/integration/test_numeric_screen.py constructs a candidate carrying (h-1/2)(h-2)(h-1/3)(h-3/7)(h-5), which vanishes at every sample point and nowhere else. It AGREES with the spec at all five points, SURVIVES the screen, and is then REJECTED by the gate. That is the asymmetry, measured.

timings_warm_interleaved.note: Five repeats, interleaved so a monotone cache or thermal trend cannot be mistaken for a difference between conditions. Caches warmed first: an earlier un-warmed run read 57.49, 21.86 and 11.57 s on three IDENTICAL invocations, a 4.97x spread, and would have supported any conclusion wanted.

result.reading: At a 50% failure rate -- where the batching model's best batch size manages 0.98x -- screening then proving is 3.10x individual verification. The INVOCATION COUNT is the robust claim: 2 against 8, flat in the failure rate, exact and noise-free. A screen invocation costs 1.39x a proof invocation, so the saving comes entirely from sharing one invocation across all b candidates, never from screening being individually cheap.

not_established: The 3.10x wall-clock exceeds the host's own 2.81x same-input spread by only about ten percent, so at five repeats the TIMING claim is thin. The invocation count is the part that does not depend on the host.
Scope: only obligations of the form 'these two functions agree pointwise' can be screened. An obligation that is not an evaluable equation must go straight to proof.

Sample points are fixed, not drawn per run, so a candidate could in principle be tuned to agree on exactly them -- which is what the constructed evader test does. That costs an isolation round and can never cause a wrong acceptance.
